In a 26.66 km ring with 450.0 GeV/c protons and a 400.8 MHz (harmonic 35640) cavity, one 60.00 s tracking call drifts the clock by 5.096×10⁻¹⁰ s, an RF phase error of 1.283 rad. An initially synchronous particle in a 6.000 MV longitudinal model ends that call at longitudinal coordinate ζ = 0.1528 m instead of 0, and resuming tracking kicks it by 5.754 MeV instead of 0. Exact integer-turn clocks establish these values; relative-time cavities and an exactly representable revolution period remain accurate.

title: Sequential step clipping violates earlier variable bounds
summary: `Line.match()` can accept an iteration that exceeds an earlier variable's `Vary.max_step`, because clipping a later variable rescales the already clipped step vector and enlarges it. title: Variable weights distort physical maximum steps
summary: Giving a matching variable a `weight` other than one changes its effective `max_step` in the variable's own units. The solver works in weighted coordinates, so converting back to the variable must convert the maximum step too, leaving the accepted physical bound independent of weight. title: CPU linked-array views bypass dependent-state updates
summary: Writing through a shared CPU slice of `Particles.delta` changes the relative momentum deviation δ without updating the dependent energy and momentum fields, so subsequent tracking uses inconsistent coordinates. Relativistic kinematics and the expanded-drift map require those fields to change together, as direct indexed assignment does. Setting a 1 GeV/c proton to δ = 0.3 through a view, then tracking 1.7 m with normalized horizontal momentum `px` = 0.0008, gives x = 1.360 mm instead of 1.046 mm. Strided views, the output of NumPy universal functions (`out=`) and aliased in-place writes also bypass updates, and slices of read-only arrays accept prohibited writes. Direct indexed assignment preserves the required consistency.

title: Copied nested fields disconnect from parent storage
summary: Copying a `SpaceChargeBiGaussian` and changing its public longitudinal-profile population leaves the tracking kernel using the old intensity, because the copied child fields are disconnected from the parent's storage. At fixed geometry the kick must scale linearly with population, as a freshly constructed control confirms. For a 0.7 m element with longitudinal RMS size 0.13 m and transverse RMS size 1.2 mm, increasing the population from 7.000×10⁹ to 1.750×10¹⁰ leaves a 1.3 GeV/c proton at the bunch center and x = 0.7 mm with normalized horizontal momentum `px` = 3.145×10⁻⁶ instead of 7.862×10⁻⁶. Both default-buffer and same-buffer copies fail. The original object remains unchanged.
